reference.title: Vulval carcinoma types
reference.intro: HPV status, not the keratinising, basaloid or warty pattern, now sets the squamous type; Squamous cell carcinoma, NOS is for when HPV status cannot be determined.

groups.heading: Squamous cell carcinoma, HPV-associated
points: Mostly basaloid or warty, but the morphology overlaps with HPV-independent carcinoma in 15 to 20 per cent
p16 block-type and p53 wild-type, often basal sparing; adjacent HSIL
A negative p16 with warty or basaloid morphology or adjacent HSIL calls for p53 or HPV testing

images.caption: HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma: sheets and nests of basaloid cells without keratinisation (H&E).
images.credit: Alsolami et al., Cancers 2026, Fig 1, panel A (cropped)

images.caption: HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma: strong, diffuse block-type staining of the tumour nests (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Alsolami et al., Cancers 2026, Fig 1, panel B (cropped)

groups.heading: Squamous cell carcinoma, HPV-independent
points: Usually keratinising, often with lichen sclerosus and chronic inflammation; verrucous carcinoma belongs here
p16 negative or patchy; p53 abnormal with adjacent dVIN, or wild-type, where verrucous morphology is over-represented

images.caption: HPV-independent squamous cell carcinoma: keratinising tumour cells infiltrating with a fibromyxoid stromal reaction (H&E).
images.credit: Peng et al., Front Oncol 2025, Fig 3, panel B (cropped)

images.caption: Keratinising squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva: infiltrating mature cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and keratin pearls (H&E).
images.credit: Léonard et al., Biomed Res Int 2014, Fig 6, full figure

images.caption: Verrucous carcinoma of the vulva: nests and islands of well-differentiated squamous cells in a dense stroma, at low power (H&E).
images.credit: Wang et al., Front Oncol 2021, Fig 1, panel A (cropped)

groups.heading: Basal cell carcinoma, NOS
points: Uncommon in the vulva

images.caption: Basal cell carcinoma of the vulva: dermal nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and clefting (H&E).
images.credit: Asuman et al., Indian J Dermatol 2008, Fig 2, full figure

groups.heading: Adenocarcinoma of anogenital mammary-like glands
points: Arises from the anogenital mammary-like glands, which can also give rise to malignant phyllodes tumours

images.caption: Mammary-type adenocarcinoma of the vulva: small glands infiltrating the dermis (H&E).
images.credit: Nobile et al., Front Oncol 2026, Fig 3, panel C (cropped)

groups.heading: Paget disease, extramammary (invasive)
points: Single cells or small groups infiltrating the dermis with a desmoplastic reaction
The invasive component may be a non-specific adenocarcinoma, a mammary-type adenocarcinoma or a sweat gland-type carcinoma

images.caption: Primary extramammary Paget disease of the vulva: pale Paget cells scattered through the epidermis (H&E).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Invasive extramammary Paget disease: Paget cells in the epidermis, with stromal and lymphovascular invasion below (arrows) (H&E).
images.credit: Alessandrini et al., Diagn Pathol 2018, Fig 1, panel b (cropped)

groups.heading: Bartholin gland carcinoma (specify the subtype)
points: Squamous cell carcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma and adenocarcinoma are the commonest subtypes
Bartholin origin: a tumour in the gland region with compatible histology, a transition from a benign gland or cyst, and no other primary site

images.caption: Squamous cell carcinoma of the Bartholin gland: irregular, anastomosing nests and cords with a brisk stromal reaction (H&E).
images.credit: Kostov et al., Cancers 2025, Fig 1, panel B (cropped)

fields.label: Morphological pattern
fields.help: Sets the description in the histology paragraph; not printed as an item. ICCR: HPV-associated carcinomas are mostly basaloid or warty, HPV-independent carcinomas mostly keratinising; verrucous carcinoma is HPV-independent.

fields.label: Histologic grade (optional)
fields.help: Optional (CAP Note E). ICCR does not recommend grading vulval squamous cell carcinoma.

reference.title: Depth of invasion: three measurements
reference.intro: Line colours: yellow, FIGO 2021; red, conventional (FIGO 2009); blue, tumour thickness. Invasion of more than 1 mm calls for groin node evaluation; say so in the report when the depth is ambiguous.

groups.heading: FIGO 2021 method
points: From the basement membrane of the deepest adjacent dysplastic, tumour-free rete ridge, or the nearest dysplastic rete peg, to the deepest point of invasion
FIGO 2021 and AJCC version 9 use it for every vulval carcinoma, whatever the type or HPV status
Where the deepest rete ridge lies deeper than the tumour, some measure from the nearest rete ridge, dysplastic or not

images.caption: Depth of invasion, the three measurements: tumour thickness (blue), the conventional depth, labelled FIGO 2009 (red), and the FIGO 2021 depth (yellow) (diagram).
images.credit: Bleeker et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2024, Fig 1 (cropped)

images.caption: FIGO 2021 method: depth (yellow) from the closest dysplastic epithelium, shorter than the conventional depth (red); preferred here by 80 per cent of the surveyed pathologists (H&E).
images.credit: Bleeker et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2024, Fig 4, panel C (cropped)

images.caption: FIGO 2021 method: an oblique depth (yellow) from the closest dysplastic epithelium to the deepest invasion, beside the conventional depth (red); the surveyed pathologists split evenly between the two (H&E).
images.credit: Bleeker et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2024, Fig 4, panel D (cropped)

groups.heading: Conventional method
points: From the epithelial-stromal junction of the most superficial adjacent dermal papilla to the deepest point of invasion (FIGO 2009)
AJCC keeps it as an ancillary value; it makes some tumours pT1b that the FIGO 2021 method stages pT1a

images.caption: Conventional method: depth (red) from the most superficial adjacent papilla; all the surveyed pathologists preferred it here, and few found the FIGO 2021 line (yellow) easy to apply (H&E).
images.credit: Bleeker et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2024, Fig 4, panel A (cropped)

groups.heading: Tumour thickness
points: From the surface of the dysplastic epithelium to the deepest point of invasion

images.caption: Tumour thickness: the blue line, from the surface to the deepest invasion, beside the conventional (red) and FIGO 2021 (yellow) depths (H&E).
images.credit: Bleeker et al., Int J Gynecol Pathol 2024, Fig 4, panel B (cropped)

fields.label: Depth of invasion, FIGO 2021 method (mm)
fields.help: FIGO 2021: from the basement membrane of the deepest adjacent dysplastic, tumour-free rete ridge (or the nearest dysplastic rete peg) to the deepest point of invasion.

fields.label: Depth of invasion, conventional method (mm, optional)
fields.help: Conventional method: from the epithelial-stromal junction of the adjacent most superficial dermal papilla. ESGO 2023 advises recording both.

fields.label: Depth of invasion cannot be determined (reason)

reference.title: Tumour border
reference.intro: Vulval squamous cell carcinomas generally either infiltrate or invade on a broad, pushing front. Tumour budding, spray-like infiltration and a fibromyxoid stromal response are related features, linked to worse outcomes in some studies but understudied as a group.

groups.heading: Pushing
points: Invasion on a broad front of rounded, bulbous nests
The pattern of verrucous carcinoma, whose nests are very well differentiated

images.caption: Pushing border: broad, bulbous nests of very well-differentiated squamous cells in verrucous carcinoma of the vulva (H&E).
images.credit: Wang et al., Front Oncol 2021, Fig 1, panel B (cropped)

images.caption: Pushing border: rounded, bulbous nests advancing on a broad front in verrucous carcinoma of the vulva (H&E).
images.credit: Bouquet de Jolinière et al., Front Surg 2016, Fig 3, panel E (cropped)

groups.heading: Infiltrating
points: Tumour buds: clusters of 4 cells or fewer detaching at the invasive front
Poorly defined clusters: 5 or more cells in the stroma at the invasive front

images.caption: Infiltrating border: tumour buds of 4 cells or fewer (arrows) detaching at the invasive front (dashed line) (H&E).
images.credit: Klamminger et al., Cancers 2025, Fig 1, panel A (cropped)

images.caption: Infiltrating border: poorly defined clusters of 5 or more cells (arrows) in the stroma at the invasive front (dashed line) (H&E).
images.credit: Klamminger et al., Cancers 2025, Fig 1, panel C (cropped)

fields.label: p16 immunohistochemistry
fields.help: Printed inside the histology paragraph. ICCR: report p16 as block-type, not simply as positive.

reference.title: p16 patterns
reference.intro: Only diffuse, block-like staining indicates HPV association; focal or patchy staining, or none, is seen in HPV-independent lesions.

groups.heading: Block-type positive
points: Strong, diffuse cytoplasmic and nuclear staining through at least the lower third of the epithelium
HPV-associated carcinoma and HSIL

images.caption: HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma: strong, diffuse block-type staining of the tumour nests (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Alsolami et al., Cancers 2026, Fig 1, panel B (cropped)

images.caption: HSIL: strong, diffuse block-type staining of the lesional epithelium (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Alsolami et al., Cancers 2026, Fig 2, panel B (cropped)

groups.heading: Patchy, non-block-type
points: Focal, patchy or mosaic staining that is not continuous
HPV-independent carcinoma and its precursors

images.caption: HPV-independent vulval squamous cell carcinoma: mosaic, non-block p16 staining (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Haddad et al., Einstein (Sao Paulo) 2025, Fig 3, panel A (cropped)

images.caption: HPV-independent, p53-wild-type VIN: patchy, non-block staining (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Thuijs et al., Cancers 2024, Fig 3, panel B (cropped)

groups.heading: Negative
points: No staining, or only rare scattered cells
Falsely negative in fewer than 1 per cent of HPV-associated carcinomas: with warty or basaloid morphology or adjacent HSIL, look for basal-sparing p53 or test for HPV

images.caption: HPV-independent, p53-wild-type squamous cell carcinoma: no staining (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Alsolami et al., Cancers 2026, Fig 1, panel N (cropped)

fields.label: p53 immunohistochemistry
fields.help: Printed inside the histology paragraph. Basal sparing (mid-epithelial) staining is the pattern of HPV-associated lesions.

reference.title: p53 patterns
reference.intro: Two wild-type and four abnormal patterns; read the basal layer first. HPV-associated carcinoma and HSIL are wild-type, often with basal sparing; an abnormal pattern goes with HPV-independent carcinoma and dVIN.

groups.heading: Wild-type pattern
points: Scattered nuclear staining of variable intensity in the basal and parabasal cells

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: scattered nuclear staining of variable intensity, a wild-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel A (cropped)

groups.heading: Wild-type, mid-epithelial (basal sparing) pattern
points: Strong to moderate staining of the middle layers, sparing the basal layer
Associated with HPV

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: mid-epithelial staining with sparing of the basal layer, a wild-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel B (cropped)

groups.heading: Abnormal, basal overexpression
points: Strong nuclear staining of consecutive basal cells; a little parabasal staining is acceptable

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: strong staining of consecutive basal cells, a mutant-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel C (cropped)

images.caption: Differentiated VIN: strong, continuous staining of the basal and parabasal layers, a mutant-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Dasgupta et al., Histopathology 2026, Fig 3, panel D (cropped)

groups.heading: Abnormal, parabasal / diffuse overexpression
points: Strong, diffuse staining of the basal and upper layers
Parabasal overexpression in more than 10 per cent of the lesion makes a basal pattern diffuse

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: strong staining from the basal into the upper layers, a mutant-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel D (cropped)

groups.heading: Abnormal, null
points: No nuclear staining, with a positive internal control

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: no nuclear staining in the tumour with positive stromal cells, a mutant-type null pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel E (cropped)

groups.heading: Abnormal, cytoplasmic
points: Diffuse cytoplasmic staining, with or without nuclear staining, and a positive internal control

images.caption: Vulval squamous cell carcinoma: diffuse cytoplasmic staining, a mutant-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Kortekaas et al., Histopathology 2020, Fig 1, panel F (cropped)

fields.label: Other immunohistochemistry
fields.placeholder: e.g. The tumour cells are positive for CK7 and GATA3.
fields.help: One sentence, printed in the histology paragraph as typed.

fields.label: Tumour histology (replaces the generated paragraph)
fields.help: Leave blank to use the paragraph built from the fields above.

fields.label: Adjacent epithelium
options: Vulvar aberrant maturation (VAM) / HPV-independent, p53-wild-type verruciform acanthotic VIN
fields.help: Printed under Additional findings; a squamous precursor or Paget disease also opens its margin field.

includes: Vulvar aberrant maturation (VAM) / HPV-independent, p53-wild-type verruciform acanthotic VIN

reference.title: Squamous precursors at a margin
reference.intro: Report the precursor margin even when invasive carcinoma involves a margin.

groups.heading: HSIL (VIN 2 or VIN 3)
points: Atypical nuclei in all layers, including the middle and upper thirds, with suprabasal and atypical mitoses
Often extends into hair follicles and skin appendages; p16 block-type, p53 wild-type

images.caption: Vulval HSIL, basaloid type: atypical parabasal-type cells through nearly the whole thickness of the epidermis (H&E).
images.credit: Léonard et al., Biomed Res Int 2014, Fig 3, full figure

images.caption: HSIL: strong, diffuse block-type staining of the lesional epithelium (p16 immunostain).
images.credit: Alsolami et al., Cancers 2026, Fig 2, panel B (cropped)

groups.heading: Differentiated VIN (dVIN)
points: Atypia confined to the basal and parabasal layers: enlarged cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli
p53 abnormal (basal, diffuse, null or cytoplasmic); p16 negative or patchy

images.caption: Differentiated VIN, deep epithelium: enlarged eosinophilic keratinocytes with atypical basal nuclei (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

images.caption: Differentiated VIN: strong, continuous staining of the basal and parabasal layers, a mutant-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Dasgupta et al., Histopathology 2026, Fig 3, panel D (cropped)

groups.heading: Vulvar aberrant maturation (VAM) / HPV-independent, p53-wild-type verruciform acanthotic VIN
points: HPV-independent lesions combining aberrant maturation and verruciform acanthosis with minimal nuclear atypia
p53 wild-type; p16 negative or non-block

images.caption: HPV-independent, p53-wild-type VIN: acanthotic epithelium with thick surface keratin (H&E).
images.credit: Thuijs et al., Cancers 2024, Fig 3, panel A (cropped)

images.caption: HPV-independent, p53-wild-type VIN: scattered basal and parabasal nuclear staining, a wild-type pattern (p53 immunostain).
images.credit: Thuijs et al., Cancers 2024, Fig 3, panel C (cropped)

Vulvar aberrant maturation (VAM) / HPV-independent, p53-wild-type verruciform acanthotic VIN

reference.title: Paget disease at a margin
reference.intro: Report the Paget disease margin even when invasive carcinoma involves a margin.

groups.heading: Paget disease (intraepithelial)
points: Enlarged cells with abundant pale cytoplasm, large nuclei and small to prominent nucleoli; intracytoplasmic mucin is frequent
Mainly basal and parabasal, extending upwards singly and in small clusters, often into skin adnexa

images.caption: Primary extramammary Paget disease of the vulva: pale Paget cells scattered through the epidermis (H&E).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

fields.label: Regional lymph nodes examined (total)
fields.help: Inguinofemoral nodes, all parts together, as CAP counts them. Leave blank when none were submitted.

fields.label: Lymph node sampling
options: Sentinel lymph node biopsy and lymphadenectomy
fields.help: Sentinel only adds (sn) to pN. A negative lymphadenectomy with fewer than 6 nodes is pN not assigned (CAP).

reference.title: Regional lymph nodes (AJCC version 9)
reference.intro: Regional nodes are inguinal and femoral; an involved iliac node is a distant metastasis (pM1).

groups.heading: Isolated tumour cells
points: 0.2 mm or less, or single cells or clusters of 200 cells or fewer in one cross-section: pN0(i+)
Counted only when no node holds a larger metastasis

groups.heading: Micrometastasis
points: More than 0.2 mm to 2.0 mm: pN1mi

groups.heading: Metastasis, by size
points: More than 2.0 mm to 5 mm: pN1a
More than 5 mm: pN1b

groups.heading: Extranodal extension and fixed nodes
points: Extranodal extension: pN1c
Fixed or ulcerated nodes: pN2

reference.note: No openly licensed photograph of a vulval carcinoma node was found, and photographs from other sites are left out.

is: Sentinel lymph node biopsy and lymphadenectomy

fields.label: Nodes with metastasis more than 5 mm
Nodes with metastasis more than 2 mm to 5 mm
Nodes with micrometastasis (more than 0.2 mm to 2 mm)
Nodes with isolated tumour cells only (0.2 mm or less)
fields.help: Counted only when no node has a metastasis larger than 0.2 mm (CAP).

fields.label: Additional lymph node findings
fields.help: Extranodal extension makes pN1c, fixed or ulcerated nodes pN2.

fields.label: Distant metastasis
fields.help: Pelvic lymph nodes are distant metastasis (pM1).

fields.label: pTNM override
fields.help: Replaces the derived pTNM; give the reason below.
